description:
I'm looking for teammates who are enthusiastic about space and open to experimenting with ideas, particularly those with skills in Python or data analysis, AI/ML, UI/UX design, astronomy, or data visualization. You don't need to be an expert—initiative, collaboration, and a willingness to learn matter just as much.

If you'd like to turn an ambitious idea into something tangible in 48 hours, let's connect and build something meaningful together!
summary: ASTRO MED-X is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring app built to support crew members during long-duration space missions where continuous real-time medical support from Earth is limited.   We developed a prototype featuring a personalized astronaut dashboard, vital signs and physical activity trackers, sleep and mental wellness check-ins, trend graphs, conditional alert logic, and offline caching for network-interrupted environments.   The application addresses spaceflight hazards like microgravity-induced deconditioning, radiation, and circadian disruption by collecting telemetry, comparing metrics against individual baselines rather than static clinical ranges, and providing clear escalation protocols.   This project is important because it empowers astronauts to safely monitor their health, recognize early warning signs autonomously, and maintain mission safety without requiring constant communication with Earth.
details: Astro Med-X is an offline-first Android crew health and environmental telemetry platform built in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (MainActivity.kt), powered by a reactive StateFlow and Kotlin Coroutines backend (AstroMergedRepository on a SupervisorJob scope). Its dual-rate telemetry worker runs a 1-second loop computing cabin pCO2 drift and Wanninkhof flux (0.378 * pCO2) alongside 1-second cardio-respiratory updates (HR, BP, SpO2, RR calibrated to CSA Bio-Monitor baselines) and 4-second metabolic/radiation updates (Temp, Sleep, Hydration, Radiation calibrated to Curiosity MSL-RAD), while polling the NASA DONKI SEP API on Dispatchers.IO for live solar particle alerts. Every packet is evaluated by BaselineRange.evaluateStatus() to dynamically recalculate CrewReadinessState scores, trigger Hypercapnia-Tachycardia alerts (CO2 > 3.0 mmHg and HR > 100 BPM), and record an AES-256-tagged delta-log with an offline sync queue for Flight Surgeon export. Creatively pairing gemini-2.5-flash REST calls with a deterministic offline RAG fallback (buildOfflineRagResponse), the backend routes every AI recommendation through SafetyInterlockEngine.validateAndEnforce() to enforce 0-g bulkhead CPR physics and NASA Flight Rule 14.2 (O2 <= 24.1%), while supporting Google OAuth 2.0 deep-link sign-in and local SharedPreferences persistence with zero hardcoded keys—enabling autonomous, privacy-preserving crew triage during deep-space communication blackouts.
